groups.spokenClause: The pair t-a occurs five times: three in stale and two in rotation

groups.name: bpe-merge
groups.spokenClause: Merging t-a turns those character pairs into one reusable token, and the tokenizer recounts the remaining pairs

groups.name: low-loss
groups.spokenClause: Assigning probability point two to that token produces about one point six nats of loss

groups.name: high-loss
groups.spokenClause: a stronger probability of point eight lowers it to about point two

groups.name: gopher-flops
groups.spokenClause: Gopher’s reported two hundred eighty billion parameters and three hundred billion tokens give about five point zero four times ten to the twenty-third FLOPs

groups.name: chinchilla-flops
groups.spokenClause: The same approximation gives five point eight eight times ten to the twenty-third FLOPs, near the Gopher estimate with a different allocation

groups.name: llama-flops
groups.spokenClause: Llama 3’s eight-billion-parameter model trained on about fifteen trillion tokens reflects a different goal: useful capability from a smaller model with recurring inference costs in view

groups.name: twenty-request-totals
groups.spokenClause: At twenty requests their totals are five and ten point five, assuming both meet the required quality

groups.name: verifier-honest-false-action
groups.spokenClause: A typed verifier rewards the honest structured fields and rejects a false action flag

groups.name: verifier-prose-contradiction
groups.spokenClause: If it ignores free-form text, a contradictory sentence can still receive reward, so the checker and user interface need broader evidence

groups.name: swapped-judge
groups.spokenClause: The outcome follows position rather than a stable preference for one answer

groups.name: candidate-pass-count
groups.spokenClause: Applying those checks to this candidate accepts two of five cases

groups.name: release-block
groups.spokenClause: Its release gate stays blocked, and the model has no twenty-case integration run

groups.name: bundle-inapplicable
groups.spokenClause: Changing just template revision four to five makes the previous bundle report inapplicable even if the weights and metric values stay the same

groups.name: bf16-storage
groups.spokenClause: Seventy billion parameters at two bytes each require about one hundred thirty point four GiB for BF16 weights alone

groups.name: int4-storage
groups.spokenClause: Ideal INT4 storage uses one quarter as many bytes, about thirty-two point six GiB before scales and runtime overhead

groups.name: two-request-subtotal
groups.spokenClause: With the stated layers, heads, dimensions, context, and two-byte cache elements, one request needs ten GiB, so two requests plus INT4 weights total fifty-two point six GiB

groups.name: device-shortfall
groups.spokenClause: That subtotal already exceeds a forty-eight-GiB device by four point six GiB

groups.name: free-memory
groups.spokenClause: A sixty-GiB teaching budget leaves seven point four GiB after those parts

groups.name: rounded-integers
groups.spokenClause: The article weights yield integers minus one hundred eleven, minus twenty-nine, seven, fifty-four and one hundred twenty-seven, with maximum reconstruction error about point zero zero two nine

groups.name: activation-output-errors
groups.spokenClause: Their output contributions are point one and point zero four; the smaller weight error has the larger effect

groups.name: toy-exact
groups.spokenClause: Weights point two four and point four four with inputs ten and one produce two point eight four

groups.name: toy-independent-round
groups.spokenClause: Independent rounding gives point two and point four, producing two point four

groups.name: toy-scaled-round
groups.spokenClause: rounding gives point five times five plus point four, or two point nine

groups.name: toy-error-improvement
groups.spokenClause: Scaling changed the rounding error from point four four to point zero six

groups.name: compensation
groups.spokenClause: In a simple input two-and-one toy, rounding the first weight down by point zero five reduces output by point one; raising the second by point one compensates before its own rounding

groups.name: static-idle
groups.spokenClause: The gap is five hundred eighty-five iterations

groups.name: token-latencies
groups.spokenClause: For a supplied trace starting at zero, output tokens at two hundred, two hundred forty and three hundred milliseconds give T T F T two hundred and inter-token gaps forty and sixty

groups.name: block-slack
groups.spokenClause: With block size four and six live tokens, two blocks have capacity eight and two unused positions

groups.name: accepted-prefix
groups.spokenClause: Emit those four and a correction sampled by the target algorithm; a later apparently good proposal cannot skip past the first rejection

groups.name: all-accepted
groups.spokenClause: If all five pass, the verification pass can also emit one bonus token

groups.name: checker-updated
groups.spokenClause: Update the application rule to sixty days, record the new version, and keep the model checkpoint fixed

groups.name: checker-boundaries
groups.spokenClause: The first stays ineligible and the second qualifies

groups.name: fresh-cache-result
groups.spokenClause: Re-evaluate the same seventy-five-day request: it is ineligible under ninety, and the action-executed flag remains false

groups.name: fresh-boundaries
groups.spokenClause: Eighty-nine is ineligible; ninety qualifies at threshold equality
